subject: Dev Connect: Invite cadence, tracking link fallback & RSVP SLO

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>

Subject: Dev Connect — invite cadence + tracking fallback idea

Team —

Quick planning note for the ACME co-hosted "Dev Connect" on Apr 14. ACME's events team will seed their list, but they want a resilient RSVP link strategy so we don't lose signals when their marketing platform and our hub have different click windows (and so Trackly can still attribute). Key asks:

- Draft short invite copy for engineers (27–35 words) + one alternative for architects.
- Build a link-fallback map: primary RSVP (ACME form), fallback (Redwood landing with prefill), and final fallback (Trackly redirect with UTM and fingerprint).
- Reminders cadence: initial invite, 3d reminder, 1d reminder, day-of quick push. Keep follow-ups thin.

I've attached the current copy draft and a blank tracking map. Can Mateo and Naomi prototype the fallback CSV? Marissa — can you produce the short copy variants and the 3 subject-line tests?

Target conversion SLO: 18% RSVP / click for seeded audience; 7% for cold acquisition. We'll monitor via Trackly map + HubSpot.

Thanks,

— Steph
Director, Field Marketing
Redwood Inference

Attachments: dev-connect-invite-copy-v3.docx, rsvp-tracking-fallback-map.csv

All —

Uploaded a first pass of the fallback map to Drive (link in metadata). Summary of the approach:

1) Primary: ACME form URL (utm_source=acme&utm_campaign=devconnect_apr14). Users who submit get added to ACME and Redwood lists via webhook.
2) Secondary (if ACME form times out / 404): Redwood landing page with prefilled e-mail query param + hidden utm_fallback=1. This has a 1-click RSVP button that writes back to Trackly.
3) Final: Trackly redirect that fingerprints the click and then attempts to open primary; if that fails after 2s it serves the Redwood landing.

Technical notes for ops: make sure the Trackly redirect preserves original click timestamp and gclid-like token for HubSpot mapping. Trackly: can you confirm we can set the redirect timeout to 1800ms (2s) and that mobile deep-linking won't break prefill?

Attachments: rsvp-tracking-fallback-map.csv

— Mateo

Redwood Inference

We'll also expose a map ID (track-539) so you can see per-link success/fallback rates. I'll send a quick dashboard invite to Naomi so she can wire HubSpot mappings.

Steph / team —

I ran a quick simulation on our tracking map and attached the CSV with expected attribution buckets. Highlights:

- Expect ~92% success on the primary ACME form for ACME-seeded test (they have a healthy platform).
- Fallback traffic should be <8% but is high-value for attribution hygiene; Trackly will label those clicks with fallback_reason "form_timeout" or "redirect_error".
- HubSpot mapping: use property "rsvp_source_fallback" to capture primary|redwood_landing|trackly_fallback. We'll need a small Zapier step for older ACME records.

Sophie — if you can confirm ACME's form webhook latency (typical 300–800ms?), we can tighten the redirect window.
